sentences.text: This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 04.05.2019 passed by Mem- ber MACT, Ujjain in Claim Case No.36/2018 on account of rejecting the claim petition and seeking compensation.
2. The brief facts of the case is that on 05.12.2016 deceased Tejsingh was going towards Badnagar on his motorcycle slowly and in the right direction.

When he reached near Fauji Dhaba a motorcycle driven by respondent no.1 bearing registration no.MP-41-M-4484 rashly and negligently hit Tejsingh due to which he suffered grievous injuries and during his treatment, he was declared dead in Apollo hospital, Ujjain.
Thereafter, claimants filed claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation against the respondents.
3. Respondent no.1 was exparte before the Tribunal and respondent no.2 filed written statement and denied all the pleadings in the claim petition.

4. The Tribunal framed the issue on the basis of the pleadings of both the parties and taking evidence of the parties and after hearing the parties, rejected the claim petition and found that the driver of the offending vehicle had not caused any accident.
5.

Being aggrieved by the said award, this appeal is filed by the claimant on the ground that Tribunal has committed error in rejecting the claim petition on the basis of delay in lodging of the FIR and further submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in disbelieving the statement of the Investigating Officer and claimants' witness Dharmendra.
Hence, prays for allowing the appeal.
6. On the other hand, the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and the findings of the Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. As per certified copy of the FIR Ex.P-2 accident occurred on 05.12.2016 and FIR was lodged on 15.12.2016.

According to the registration of unnatural death under Section 174 of Cr.P.C.Ex.P-3,
Merg intimation was registered at the police station on 15.12.2016.

According to Ex.P-5 Rojnamchasanha dated 05.12.2016, it is found that information was received in the Police Station Badnagar, district Ujjain that injured Tejsingh was taken to hospital due to road accident.
He was referred for further treatment to District Hospital, Ujjain.
MLC was done vide Ex.P-6 on 05.12.2016.
The information was sent to the police by the duty doctor on 13.12.2016 to Police Station Neelganga that Tejsingh died during treatment.
9. It is settled principle of law that delay in filing FIR is not fatal either in criminal cases or in claim cases provided sufficient and cogent reasons for delay in filing the FIR.

In the case of Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226 the Apex Court has held as under:-
"20.

entities.text:
Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we can-not expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."
10. It reveals from the record that from the date of accident till death of the deceased, the deceased was admitted in the hospital.
On perusal of the evidence of the claimants' deceased was alone driving the motorcycle and no family member or his friend was with him.

In the certified copy of Rojnamchasanha dated 05.12.2016 Ex.P-5 it is clearly stated that Tejsingh received injury in road Smt. Radhabai vs Bharatsingh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131771223/
3 accident and admitted in Badnagar hospital and he was referred for further treatment to Ujjain hospital.
So the information was received by the police on same date.
It is the duty of police to enquire the matter but the police have not enquired the matter till 09.01.2017.

11. Witness AW-1 Sabir Hussain was examined by the Insurance Company and he was the Investigating Officer of the alleged crime and he after due investigation filed charge sheet before the Criminal Court.
He stated in his evidence that he took the statement of Dharmendra, Rakesh and Gokul on 09.01.2017.
12. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company stated that Dharmendra AW-2 had not dared to come before the police station to inform that he saw the registration number of the offending vehicle.
In this regard, perusal of evidence of Dharmendra it is found that Dharmendra is not relative, family member or friend of the deceased.
So a common man who fulfilled his duty on humanitarian ground did not felt it necessary to go to the police station for giving information regarding the registration number of the offending vehicle.
He did not know the legal requirement of the case.
13. Considering the evidence of AW-2 he was intact in his cross examination hence he was not telling lie or that he was interested in the claimants.

On perusal of the mechanical report Ex.P-15, it is found that the offending vehicle was damaged and no explanation was given by the driver or owner of the offending vehicle as to how the offending vehicle was damaged.

It is the duty of the police/Investigating Officer to take steps for searching the registration number of the offending vehicle but from 05.12.2016 till 09.01.2017 no steps were taken by the police for searing the registration number of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it is the fault of the police and not the claimants.

14. In the case of Gayatribai Vs. Narendra reported in 1999 (II) MPWN S.N.141 it was held by the Division Bench of this Court that respondent did not examine the driver to reveal the circumstances of the accident and negligence on the part of driver may be inferred.

entities.text: Gayatribai Vs. Narendra reported in 1999 (II) MPWN S.N.141
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. In the present case, Insurance Company had not called driver of the offending vehicle for deposing evidence before the Tribunal and information of accident had been received by the police on the same date and it is also not disputed that no family member of the deceased was present with him at the time of accident and eye witness Dharmendra is not relative, friend or family member of the deceased.
So he had not bothered to lodge FIR promptly.
16. Hence, it is found that delay in lodging the FIR had sufficiently been explained by the claimants.

So delay to lodge FIR has not fatal the case and driver/owner of the offending vehicle had not dared to come before the Tribunal to adduce evidence as to how the accident had occurred and he is not responsible for the accident.
17. In view of the aforesaid discussions, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has committed error in holding that accident had not occurred by the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal in this regard is bad in law and deserves to be set aside.

Hence, it is proved Smt. Radhabai vs Bharatsingh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131771223/
4 that driver of the offending vehicle had caused the accident due to which the deceased received injuries and during treatment he died.

sentences.text: 18. On perusal of the award, it is found that Tribunal has not assessed the amount of compensation.

Therefore, this matter is remanded back to the Tribunal to consider the matter afresh and after hearing the parties, if necessary, take evidence and assess the amount of compensation to the claimants with regard to the death of the deceased.
Parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 12.03.2024.
With the aforesaid, this appeal stands disposed off.
